title.zh: 分子氢电荷交换Maxwellian速率系数

summary: Evaluate the H2 + H2+ charge-exchange Maxwellian rate-coefficient fit from paired plasma temperature and impact energy samples in eV.

capability: Maxwellian H2 + H2+ charge-exchange rate coefficient from paired temperature and impact-energy samples in eV.
operation: Evaluate the molecular-H2 charge-exchange Maxwellian rate coefficient
paired plasma temperature and impact energy in eV -> rate coefficient in m^3/s
discovery.model: Molecular-H2 nine-by-nine bivariate logarithmic rate fit; not a velocity-mesh Maxwellian integral.
discovery.geometry: None; paired scalar or array material samples with no spatial or velocity axis inferred (coordinates: temperature and impact energy in eV).
discovery.boundary: Inputs must be finite and identically shaped with strictly positive temperature and nonnegative impact energy; both dimensions clip at the fit endpoints and the output must be finite and positive.

identity.relation: molecular-H2 charge-exchange Maxwellian rate coefficient from a bivariate logarithmic fit
identity.direction: paired plasma temperature and impact energy in eV -> rate coefficient in m^3/s
identity.definition: Sequentially clip positive temperature and nonnegative impact energy to [0.1, 2.01e4] eV. With L_T=log(T), L_E=log(E), accumulate log_rate=sum_j=0..8 sum_i=0..8 a[i,j]*L_E^j*L_T^i using the energy-outer, temperature-inner addition order and the molecular 9x9 coefficient table. Return exp(log_rate)*1e-6 m^3/s. The output keeps the paired input shape.
identity.model: Molecular-H2 nine-by-nine bivariate logarithmic rate fit; not a velocity-mesh Maxwellian integral
identity.geometry: none; paired scalar or array material samples
identity.coordinates: temperature and impact energy in eV, with no spatial or velocity axis inferred
identity.boundary: finite real numeric inputs of identical shape; temperature strictly positive, impact energy nonnegative; endpoint clipping in both dimensions, with RuntimeWarning above the upper edge; finite positive represented output
assumptions: The molecular coefficient table and summation order define the fit on finite real inputs.

The atomic-H charge-exchange rate is a distinct physical system with another coefficient table. The molecular fit also does not call the molecular cross-section fit or maxwellian-relative-speed-rate-average; their equivalence is not established.
The callable requires exact shape equality between temperature and energy; broadcast-compatible input shapes are not supported.
Nonpositive temperature, negative energy and boolean or numeric-string coercions are rejected.

inputs.name: temperature_ev
inputs.description: Plasma temperature for the molecular Maxwellian rate fit.
inputs.shape: scalar or array; exactly the shape of energy_ev
inputs.constraints: Finite and strictly positive; values below 0.1 eV are clipped silently; values above 2.01e4 eV are clipped to the upper endpoint and emit RuntimeWarning.

inputs.name: energy_ev
inputs.description: Impact energy paired with each temperature sample.
inputs.shape: scalar or array; exactly the shape of temperature_ev
inputs.constraints: Finite and nonnegative; zero and positive values below 0.1 eV are clipped silently; values above 2.01e4 eV are clipped to the upper endpoint and emit RuntimeWarning.

outputs.name: rate_m3_s
outputs.description: H2 + H2+ charge-exchange Maxwellian rate coefficient evaluated by the molecular fit.
outputs.constraints: Finite and strictly positive on accepted inputs; no physical reference accuracy is asserted.

preconditions: The caller accepts the endpoint-clipping convention and supplies physically paired temperatures and impact energies.
supported: Scalar and equal-shape array evaluation of the molecular-H2 charge-exchange rate fit on or clipped to its declared domain.
excluded: Atomic-H charge exchange, molecular elastic scattering, dissociation, CX collision-frequency assembly and explicit velocity-mesh averaging of a cross section.
External atomic-physics accuracy claims or physical correctness outside the fit's compared domain.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for non-real numeric, non-finite or unequal-shape inputs, nonpositive temperature or negative energy. Boolean, complex and numeric-string coercions are rejected.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises ValueError if the derived rate is non-finite or nonpositive; no partial output is returned.

example.description: Evaluate the molecular fit and compare it with the distinct atomic fit.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.collisions import evaluate_hydrogen2_charge_exchange_rate, evaluate_atomic_hydrogen_charge_exchange_rate
t = np.array([0.1, 10.0, 20100.0])
e = np.array([0.2, 10.0, 20100.0])
r = evaluate_hydrogen2_charge_exchange_rate(t, e)
a = evaluate_atomic_hydrogen_charge_exchange_rate(t, e)
assert r.shape == (3,) and np.all(np.isfinite(r)) and np.all(r > 0.0)
assert not np.allclose(r, a, rtol=1e-12, atol=0.0)
example.expected: Three positive molecular rates, numerically distinct from the atomic-H fit on the same pairs.

scope: Fixed reference values and independent polyval2d reevaluation verify the molecular coefficient direction and fit on ordinary samples; the double-upper-endpoint corner is checked against the declared-order value.
Direct tests cover molecular-vs-atomic difference, clipping, scalar shape, invalid domain and non-real input rejection.

No external implementation comparison is maintained or replayed by this repository; the maintained tests validate the declared relation against an in-repository independent formulation and cover the stated rejection and clipping behaviour only on their tested grids.
verification.evidence_ceiling: The tests establish the discrete fit, clipping and failure contract on tested samples. Bit-exact agreement with the in-file independent evaluation of the same expressions holds on the compared grids only. No external atomic-physics oracle validates the fit; public distribution licensing is absent.
known_limitations: No external atomic-physics oracle is bound; the fit is not independently validated as a physical rate model.
Out-of-fit-range values silently repeat endpoint rates rather than extrapolating or failing.
The fitted rate is not derived at runtime from the separate molecular cross-section asset or the mesh rate-average asset.
No environment-gated external-implementation comparison exists in this repository; any earlier external comparison is not replayed by the maintained tests.

The frozen bivariate fit is non-monotonic in impact energy: at 1000 eV, over 500 logarithmically spaced energies in [0.1, 2.01e4] eV, its log-derivative changes sign four times and its minimum/maximum ratio is about 0.28. This is a fit property, not a validated physical threshold; callers must not assume a monotone rate.
